blocks.title: Permanent dipole-permanent dipole force
blocks.text: The force of attraction between the positive end of a polar molecule and the negative end of a nearby polar molecule is called the permanent dipole-permanent dipole force (pd-pd).

blocks.alt: Top: four polar molecules in a row, each with a d+ end and a d- end, attracting head to tail. Middle: HCl molecules lined up so H (d+) of one faces Cl (d-) of the next, joined by dashed attractions. Bottom: two chloroform molecules, CHCl3, the H (d+) of one attracted to a Cl of the next.
blocks.caption: Permanent dipole - permanent dipole forces in HCl and chloroform (original diagram after Figure 5.3).

blocks.text: Whenever HCl molecules are close to each other, as in the liquid state, they tend to line up, positive end to negative end. Similar forces are present among the molecules of chloroform, CHCl3, which has a positive centre at the hydrogen atom and a negative centre on the end with the chlorine atoms.
